prioritized_defects.description: The save-trade-information action is modeled in the Security Account Management lane, but the requirement assigns the save action to Security Account Management after CTS outputs the successful trade information. The current control flow makes the CTS node N19 feed directly into N20, which is consistent, but the diagram also presents this as a normal continuation of the main CTS workflow rather than the separately triggered post-trade saving use case; the semantic issue is that the lane and trigger relation for saving trade information are not aligned with the requirement's actor/trigger separation.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R41 states CTS "give out the successful trade information" and R42 states "security account management: save the trade information". In the diagram, N19 is in Central Trading System and N20 is in Security Account Management, with E26 connecting them directly in one uninterrupted activity chain. This collapses the separate use-case trigger/hand-off into the same workflow and does not reflect the requirement's separation between CTS output and Security Account Management saving as a distinct receiving activity.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Model the CTS handoff to Security Account Management as a distinct message/transfer or separate triggered interaction, and keep the save action clearly owned by Security Account Management rather than an inline CTS continuation.
Connect all diagram nodes to the main workflow.
